title: Shared genetic basis and structure of syndromic and normal facial variation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the FaceBase ERMrest API record for dataset FB00000861 (DOI 10.25550/TJ0): it states 'This is restricted-access human data' with protected_human_subjects=true and an access process via FaceBase data guidelines. Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500; supplement endpoint returned no zip.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Syndromic sample size (n = 2,596 scans: 436 Creaform plus 2,160 3dMDFace), 66 syndromes, and use of non-syndromic genotyped cohorts came from the abstract and a search-result summary of the data availability statement. Non-syndromic genotypes are on dbGaP (e.g. phs000949, 'Genetic Analysis of Normal Human Facial Variation'), which is controlled access; not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked in the FaceBase record: the 3D facial scans (FB00000861) are restricted-access human data that need an application. Normal-cohort genotypes sit in dbGaP (database of Genotypes and Phenotypes), also controlled access.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked: the files could not be opened. Inputs would be raw .ply 3D meshes that need landmarking or registration.

existing_models.name: Hallgrimsson et al. 2020, automated syndrome diagnosis from 3D facial imaging (Genetics in Medicine)
existing_models.score_and_split: Per search summary: 48.8% top-1 and 87.2% top-10 accuracy across 397 classes (396 syndromes plus controls); 96% of unaffected subjects classified correctly. Split not checked.

existing_models.name: Triplet-based singular geometric autoencoder, a 3D clinical face phenotype space of syndromes (PMC12346114)
Deep invertible 3D facial shape model for interpretable syndrome diagnosis (PMC9429803)

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: the data are controlled access.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use 3D face scans to predict which genetic syndrome a person has and how strongly their face shows it.
plain_idea.train_on: About 2,596 3D facial scans of people with 66 syndromes, plus scans of unaffected relatives (count from the paper; files not opened).
plain_idea.predict: The clinical syndrome diagnosis and position along a syndrome-specific face-shape axis. The diagnosis comes from clinical and molecular genetic records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinical geneticists could triage undiagnosed patients faster. This is already done by existing models, and the data need an access application.

more_or_better_data.why: Hallgrimsson et al. 2020 already trained on the same FaceBase collection (3,327 syndromic subjects, 396 syndromes), which is larger than this paper's 2,596 scans.

confidence_score.why: Not assessable without access. No replicate scans were confirmed.

models_beatable.why: The 2020 model reached 48.8% top-1 accuracy, which leaves room, but later geometric autoencoder models (2022–2025) exist and their splits were not checked.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No open baseline weights were confirmed, and the data themselves are behind an access application.

ml_idea: Syndrome classification or severity regression from 3D facial meshes. Blocked by restricted access to FaceBase and dbGaP.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the data are inaccessible without an application.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: FaceBase FB00000861 record says restricted access. Already failed.

verdict_reason: A1 fails. The FaceBase record (checked via its API) marks the 3D facial scans (FB00000861) as restricted-access human-subject data needing an application, and the genotypes are in dbGaP. Controlled access; the task is also already modelled on the same collection.
